text: Northfield Health Network, a fictional regional healthcare system, has six hospital sites, each running Fabric independently — and three different numbers for the same metric, with a compliance audit six weeks away.

Six sites, no shared structure, each with its own workspace and its own copy of patient data. Three different versions of Patient Readmission Rate, and an audit that will ask for exactly one traceable answer.

Chapters 1 through 3: the admin establishes real domains with their own capacity, moves everyone onto one shared, shortcut-linked Lakehouse instead of six copies, and locks it down — row-level security per site, PHI columns labeled, every access logged.

Chapters 4 and 5: the compliance team's version gets certified, so it's the one people actually find and build on — lineage traced, impact checked before anyone touches a column. Sites still self-serve new reports off that one certified model, and the whole Fabric estate gets scanned into the same Purview catalog as the legacy claims database.

Six weeks later, the audit gets a real answer: one certified model, traced lineage, per-site security, and a logged trail — not because anyone rebuilt the data, but because every layer pointed at the same source. Next: the practice lab, where you apply this yourself.
